query.description: Delete even though the device is online, and ask its agent to release its adoption identity

request.description: Delete a specific node (account-scoped). A node whose device is ONLINE is refused with 409 unless force=true: deleting it there strands the device, which keeps retrying with an identity the platform no longer knows. A forced delete also asks the agent to release its own adoption file (agent >= 0.5.0) so the device is left clean. Either way the deletion is recorded under GET /api/v1/nodes/deleted and the node can be restored from there.

Devices this account's install flow turned away because their hardware serial is registered to another account. The device only receives a vague refusal and keeps retrying, so this is how the person on Add Node learns why nothing appears. Derived at read time from the platform's refusal record: `live` = refused within the last few minutes (still powered on and retrying), `still_bound_elsewhere` = the serial is held by another account right now. Names the serial only, never the owning account. Requires node.create.

Nodes that were deleted and whose device may still be running. Deleting a node removes the row and tells the DEVICE nothing: it keeps retrying with an identity the platform no longer knows, and a network-first one cannot even reach recovery. The unique token is never returned. Requires node.delete.

Re-creates the node under its ORIGINAL id, token and boot override, so the device still carrying that identity is accepted again. Restores an identity only — command history, tracked files, secret attachments and workflow runs stay gone. 409 if it was already restored, a live node holds that id, or the hardware serial has since been registered to another account (code `serial_bound_elsewhere`): a deleted node's serial is free for anyone to bind, and restoring one that moved would return a record no device can reach. A node that was admitted when it was deleted is admitted again by its restore, under the device cap: at the cap the restore is refused with 409 (code `device_cap_reached`, the numbers in `data`), or at the account's own device limit (code `account_device_limit_reached`), and the record stays restorable until a slot is free. 503 `device_cap_unverified` = the device cap could not be checked; nothing was written, try again. Requires node.delete.

Drops the deleted-node record. After this the device cannot be taken back without physical access — which is the point: while the record exists, anyone who can delete a node can also bring that device back onto the account. Requires node.delete.
Create a secondary/backup node
Download adoption file for a node (contains node credentials including unique_token for agent registration)
Download a per-node SD/USB provisioning bundle (ZIP) baked with this node's per-node token. The device binds to this node on first boot and comes up already approved.

exec: // The ticket is what Adopt Node via SSH presents; it is bound to this
// account, user, host and port and expires 15 minutes after the probe.

request.description: Non-destructive SSH connectivity/capability probe (reachability, host key, arch, sudo, CDN). Requires ssh_adopt.enabled. A reachable probe returns host_key_ticket (stored in device_host_key_ticket; valid 15 minutes) which Adopt Node via SSH presents, and host_key_fingerprint (stored in device_host_key_fingerprint). A probe with no expected_host_key_fingerprint answers first_contact=true. With the variable set, a later probe checks the device still presents that key: host_key_changed=true otherwise, with both fingerprints, no ticket, and no credential offered. To accept a reinstalled device's new key, keep the expectation and send accept_new_host_key=true once: the result carries host_key_reset=true and a ticket for the new key, and the audit trail records both fingerprints. 429 preflight_capacity = the server (8) or this account (4) already runs that many probes.

Start an async SSH adoption: install the agent, register the node, wait for connect and (optionally) flash a network-first EEPROM. Reboots the device. Returns a job; poll Get Adoption Job. The adoption never accepts a host key on first use: send exactly one of host_key_ticket (from SSH Preflight, run it first; valid 15 minutes and bound to your account, user, host and port) or host_key_fingerprint (the device's SHA256 host key known out of band, e.g. the device_host_key_fingerprint variable). The connection is strict against that key and a different key fails before any credential is offered. 400 host_key_binding_required = neither was sent, or the ticket expired or was issued for another host, port, account or user; run SSH Preflight again. 429 adoption_capacity = the server (4) or this account (2) already runs that many adoptions; wait and retry, no job was created. 409 `device_cap_reached` = the install is at its device cap; 409 `account_device_limit_reached` = the account is at its own device limit; 503 `device_cap_unverified` = the cap could not be checked; try again. Neither creates a job.

On a server where SSH adoption is off this answers 400 (code ssh_adopt_disabled), the same refusal the preflight gives.
Current state + per-step progress of an SSH adoption run.
Connect a node (called by agent, no auth required). Requires node_id, account_id, unique_token, and hardware fingerprint.

WebSocket upgrade. Gated by TERMINAL_ENABLED + account ownership. After connect, send {"token":"<jwt>","cols":80,"rows":24}; then {"type":"input","data":"..."} or {"type":"resize","cols":..,"rows":..}. Not exercisable via plain Postman REST.
Ids of the nodes the authenticated user marked as favorite (per-user, no policy semantics)
Mark or unmark a node as the authenticated user's favorite

Returns the overclock preset catalog (stock/balanced/performance with their config.txt directives) for the node's detected board (Pi 4 / CM4 / Pi 5 / CM5). board is empty and presets is [] when the node's model has no catalog

Resolves the named preset for the node's board and dispatches a patch_file command writing it into a managed marker block in /boot/firmware/config.txt. item.name: Provision EEPROM (netboot identity / boot order / bootloader update)

request.description:
Signs a fresh per-device EEPROM image (latest firmware base, per-serial HTTP_PATH, adoption token, requested boot order) and commands the online node to flash it. Body is optional: omit boot_order for the network-first default (http,nvme,sd,restart). On a managed OS a reboot is required after the command completes.

A node that has not reported its hardware serial yet answers 409 (code no_hardware_serial).

Returns the newest bootloader firmware (version hash, build timestamp, image name) the EEPROM signer would bake from, keyed by SoC (cm4/cm5). Used by the UI to tell whether a node's running bootloader is up to date.
Generic RPIBOOT second-stage (recovery.bin) for the given SoC (cm4|cm5), proxied from the EEPROM signer. Used by the browser WebUSB flasher to boot a device in nRPI_BOOT into file-server mode.

Match-or-create a node by hardware serial (short USB serial OK), bake its adoption token into a signed network-first EEPROM package and return the file list + package base URL for the browser WebUSB flasher. An empty node_name falls back to Node-<serial>; empty credentials stay empty — the node gets no provisioning account and no console password until an operator sets them. The node is created in the "flashing" state and revealed as ready_for_adoption only via the commit endpoint below.

Finalize a WebUSB flash: reveal a node held in the "flashing" state as ready_for_adoption once the browser confirms the EEPROM write completed. Idempotent — a node that already advanced (e.g. the device connected first) is left untouched.
Deployment capability flags (ssh_adopt, eeprom_signer, netboot, sd_provisioning, terminal, one_command_adopt). A hosted install lacks same-network features; the UI hides them based on this map.

The install's device entitlement: state (free | active | grace | lapsed | rejected), the free device cap, the effective cap admission enforces now (0 = unlimited), the install-wide admitted device count (admitted_devices, every account counted), the caller's own account's admitted count (account_devices), the file in force (customer_id, kind, device_cap, issued_at, expires_at, grace_days, grace_until, note) and any offered file that did not verify. Instance-wide. Requires entitlement.manage (super_admin). That full card goes to the account that operates the install (the oldest account; instance_operator=true); any other account's super_admin gets the summary only (state, the caps, account_devices, expires_at, grace_until) and never the customer, kind, note, source, rejections or the install-wide admitted_devices. Both are mode=instance. With a per-account device limit set (ACCOUNT_DEVICE_LIMIT), any account other than the instance operator gets mode=account_limit instead: its own account_device_limit (0 = none, -1 = unreadable), account_plan (free | subscription), account_plan_until (a dated subscription only), account_devices and account_limit_contact, and nothing of the install's entitlement.

header.description: Step-up proof from POST /api/v1/auth/reauth/password (or the passkey or OIDC step-up).

request.description: Applies a signed entitlement file (the paste form, entl1.<payload>.<signature>) to the install. Verified against the keys built into the server; the newest valid file wins, so pasting the next file extends or upgrades and revokes nothing. A file that does not verify is refused with 400 (code entitlement_rejected) and nothing is stored. Requires entitlement.manage (super_admin), a recent step-up confirmation, and that the caller's account operates the install (the oldest account); any other account is refused with 403 (code not_instance_operator). The answer is the entitlement now in force plus `applied`, the pasted file's own terms: a valid file is stored even when it does not take effect (issued before a file still active or in grace, or already lapsed), so the top-level terms can be another file's. `applied` carries in_force (is the pasted file the one in force now), issued_at, expires_at, device_cap (0 = unlimited) and state (its own phase: active | grace | lapsed); it is on this answer only, never on GET.
PUBLIC. POSIX installer served for `curl -fsSL <platform>/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- --token '<adoption-blob>'`. 404 when the agent CDN is unavailable (non-local storage).

item.name: Scan OS users on a node

request.description: Dispatches a fixed read-only scan of the device's real OS login accounts (distinct from Orchestrator-managed access entries). Requires node.credentials_read. Returns command_id to poll. Online-only.
Returns the parsed OS-account inventory (status running/completed/failed). Raw output is parsed server-side and never returned.
Dispatches a read of the actually-flashed rpi-eeprom-config (BOOT_ORDER, NET_INSTALL_*, HTTP_HOST/PATH). Requires node EEPROM-flash rights. Returns command_id to poll. Online-only, RPi only.
Returns the parsed live EEPROM config (status running/completed/failed).

Returns the node's watchdog state: desired config + desired_hash, applied_hash + in_sync (what the device confirmed), queued (converge accepted but not yet delivered - an offline/netbooted node receives it on reconnect), last_command (newest apply_watchdog_config command: id/status/details), disarm_reason (the agent's on-device breaker took the watchdog down), last_refusal (the agent's pre-arm verification declined the config, '<code>: <details>'), public_ping_targets, and recovery_limited (config enabled but a watchdog reboot loop has no netboot failsafe behind it on this node).

Arms the watchdog from a named preset: agent-health (safest default), os-hang, network (also requires ping_target), or full. Validates, stores desired state and dispatches the converge command; the agent verifies the config on-device before arming and refuses one that would reboot-loop the node (the refusal appears as last_refusal in the state). Queueable: an offline node gets it on reconnect (response has queued=true - accepted, NOT applied). Requires agent >= 0.4.0 and a managed OS (held while netbooted). 400 on validation failure or agent too old.

Arms the watchdog from an explicit WatchdogConfig body (what the UI's Re-arm re-PUTs). Same validation and dispatch path as the preset form; domain bounds apply (hardware timeout 5-15s, interval < timeout, agent window 120-3600s, 1-4 IP ping targets, load limits >= 2, temperature 60-110C). The platform always forces on-device pre-arm verification regardless of the payload.

Disables supervision on the device while keeping the stored configuration for a later re-enable (dispatches the converge with enabled=false). Disarming is always allowed - a disabled config needs no validation.

The four supervision presets with the operator wording that belongs with them (label, description, and the consequence sentence a confirmation must show) and the config each expands to. The network entry carries requires_ping_target=true and an empty ping_targets - it needs an address before it can be armed - and its consequence contains the literal placeholder {{target}} for that address. node.read; the catalog is node-independent today, the route is node-scoped for authorization.

Dispatches a fixed read-only script that reads the live watchdog state off the DEVICE - whether watchdog.service is running, whether /dev/watchdog attached, the agent's breaker state and the age of the agent liveness file. Answers what the stored state cannot: a watchdog stopped by hand on the node, which the platform would otherwise keep reporting as 'in sync'. Returns command_id to poll. Online-only; no agent version floor (run_script). Requires node.status_check, NOT node.read: the probe is read-only on the device but it still dispatches a command the agent executes and flips the node to `maintenance` while it runs, which a viewer role must not be able to cause.

Returns the parsed probe once the agent reports (status running/completed/failed). The poll is bound to the node AND to the exact fixed probe script, so an arbitrary command id cannot be used to read another run_script's stdout; raw output is never returned. Also requires node.status_check. `breaker_disarmed` means the DEVICE's own breaker tripped; `disarmed_by_platform` means supervision is simply switched off because the platform asked — the two used to be indistinguishable.

The hardware registry: carrier-board profiles (fixed peripherals, factory variants, expansion ports) and attachable modules (bus needs, overlays, capabilities). Tenant-independent, served verbatim - authed but action-free.

The effective equipage (resolved node -> OU -> root -> account with the source level), per-option declared/applied/confirmed statuses, granted capabilities, applied + desired render hashes, compatible profile ids for the picker, and the HAT identity the last scan reported.

Declares the node's own equipage (profile + factory variant + which module in which port). Validated against the registry - unknown ids, module/port fit, bus and I2C-address conflicts, board compatibility - and refused on any violation. Empty profile_id clears the declaration (falls back to OU/account inheritance). Stores only: nothing reaches the device until an explicit apply. node.file_write.

The exact config.txt managed-block content an apply would write, its hash, and the typed setup steps - the confirm dialog's content, produced by the same render the apply uses. reboot_required is always true.

Dispatches apply_device_profile: ONE queueable, managed-OS-only command (config.txt block + typed setup steps, one terminal status). Offline/netbooted nodes queue it for the next managed-OS connect (queued=true, no command_id). Requires agent >= 0.6.0 (fail-closed). A reboot is required afterwards and never performed automatically. node.file_write.

Dispatches the fixed read-only hardware probe (TPM/RTC device nodes, HAT ID EEPROM); returns command_id to poll. Refused while the node runs the netboot recovery image. Detection only CONFIRMS the declaration. node.status_check.

Reads a dispatched scan; once the agent reports, the parsed result (paths present, HAT identity) is persisted as the node's scan state - what turns 'applied' into 'confirmed'/'not confirmed'. The command must be the fixed scan this endpoint dispatches.

Blinks the node's locate LED (sysfs ACT fallback on any Pi; boards with digital LEDs get their configured rendering). Agent reports success immediately and stops on its own timer (default 30 s, max 120); a repeat call restarts it. Not queueable - offline fails fast. Requires agent >= 0.6.0. node.status_check.
Gets a specific node command by ID

Mints a short-lived single-use code for the node's one-command install link; the device exchanges it over TLS for the adoption config. Re-minting revokes the previous code. The link no longer carries the adoption blob (account id, topology, reusable credential).

Approves a node that is pending approval (registered via master token). Approving admits the device under the device cap: 409 `device_cap_reached` at the cap, 409 `account_device_limit_reached` at the account's own device limit, 503 `device_cap_unverified` when the cap could not be checked (try again); either way the node stays pending.
Clears the "auto-recovered" boot-loop failsafe flag and the withheld-attempt counter for a node (operator acknowledge).
Sends a command (reboot, shutdown, status_check) to a node

formdata.description: Image file to upload (ISO, IMG, etc.)

request.description: Upload a file for an image. The file will be stored and FileStorageInfo will be updated. Re-uploading will replace the old file. The upload is ADMITTED before the body is read: 404 for an image the account does not own, 409 when an upload or compression already holds the record, and 429 (code upload_capacity) when the server or this account is at its concurrent-upload bound — wait and retry. The stored object is always application/octet-stream regardless of the part's Content-Type, and /cdn serves it as an attachment.

response.name: Success Response

request.description: Mint a short-lived, self-authenticating URL for the image bytes, so an account can take an uploaded or captured image back out of the platform. Returns the URL, not the file. Requires image MANAGE, not merely read — a captured image is a whole-disk snapshot. The URL needs no Authorization header and expires in 15 minutes; /cdn serves no Range requests, so a broken transfer needs a fresh URL. 409 if the image has no stored file yet (a capture still uploading).

Download an image file via the CDN endpoint. This endpoint only works with local storage. The file path should be set from the Upload Image File response (stored in image_file_path variable). No authentication required.

Starts background compression of an uploaded image file to the deploy format — multi-block xz (zstd fallback). Raw files (.img/.iso) are compressed; .zst uploads and single-block .xz uploads are repacked (multi-block xz decompresses in parallel on devices). By default the original file is KEPT in storage and referenced via file_storage_info.source_file_path; with image.replace_original_on_compress the original is deleted after a successful compression instead. Files already in the deploy format are final. Progress is reported in compression_status/compression_progress.

Create a new master token and download a ZIP bundle (boot-partition files + node-adoption.txt) to unzip onto a FAT32 SD card or USB drive for provisioning a factory-clean device. Response is application/zip; save it to a file.

Create an OU. Omit/null parent_id for a root unit; set to a root OU to nest one level. Policies: inherit|on|off. Every policy the update takes is accepted here with the same meaning: position, the provisioning defaults, device_profile, led_config and watchdog_config.

A policy flag outside inherit, on, off, or a watchdog, LED or device-profile config the validator refuses, answers 400 with the reason (codes invalid_policy_flag, invalid_watchdog_config, invalid_led_config, invalid_device_profile), and no unit is created; an unknown os_image_id or ssh_key_id answers 400 too.

parent_id: omit=unchanged, ""=make root, <root-uuid>=nest (two levels max). position: sibling sort order.

A policy flag outside inherit, on, off, or a watchdog, LED or device-profile config the validator refuses, answers 400 with the reason (codes invalid_policy_flag, invalid_watchdog_config, invalid_led_config, invalid_device_profile); an unknown os_image_id or ssh_key_id answers 400 too.
Fails if the OU still has nested units or assigned nodes.

A flag outside inherit, on, off answers 400 (code invalid_policy_flag) and nothing is written.
Resolved policy walking node -> OU -> root -> default, with source.
Account-wide policy fallback applied to unassigned nodes and any field the OU chain leaves unresolved

Update the account-wide policy fallback. Omitted fields are unchanged; empty string / "inherit" clears a field back to unset.

Same refusals as the OU update (400 with a code). The response carries the updated_at the save wrote.

One-call overview for the Organization page: the unit, its effective (inherited) policy with sources, counts, a fleet-push impact number, and first-N samples of nodes, access entries, secrets, playbooks and adoption tokens. Sections the caller's role cannot read are absent and named in `omitted`.

Clears every per-node policy override (boot flags, SSH password login, provisioning defaults, hardware platform, LED behaviour) so the node inherits from its unit chain again. Pushes the access config to the node when an SSH password login override was cleared.

item.name: Access Entries
item.description: Declarative shell access: named OS users with key sets, plus trusted external CAs. Lifecycle is derived — an empty key set locks the user rather than deleting it. All endpoints require the access.manage permission.

request.description: A named OS user with a set of SSH keys. An empty key set means the user is LOCKED on the node (account expired, home kept), not deleted. Password is optional: when absent, sudo is granted NOPASSWD, because a key-only user would otherwise have no credential to authenticate sudo with.

item.name: Create user access entry with password

request.description: With a password set, sudo prompts for it. The value is encrypted at rest and never returned by any endpoint — responses report has_password only.
Trusts an EXTERNAL CA (e.g. a corporate one). We issue no certificates; we only accept ones this CA signed, bounded by principals. Without principals a trusted CA could vouch for any name it signs.

item.name: List access entries for an OU
List access entries for a node

request.description: Per-OU entry counts for the credentials filter rail, plus the account-default (unattached) count and the total.
Omitted fields are left unchanged. clear_password is separate from password because an empty string cannot distinguish 'leave it' from 'remove it'.
Removes the password. sudo then becomes NOPASSWD for this user, since no credential remains to prompt for.

item.name: Attach a key to an entry

request.description: Per-key rather than a whole-list PUT: replacing the set would let a stale client wipe keys it never saw. Attach the new key BEFORE detaching the old one to rotate without a window where the user is locked.

item.name: Detach a key from an entry

request.description: Detaching the last key LOCKS the user on the next apply — the account and its home directory survive; only login is removed. Re-attaching a key unlocks it.

item.name: Get effective access for a node

request.description: The resolved union across node > OU > root OU > account, with provenance. Within one username the nearest scope overrides entirely; the entries it shadowed are reported in `overridden` so nothing disappears silently.

item.name: Re-apply access config on a node

request.description: Manually re-pushes the node's effective access configuration to the device (self-heal after a failed or stale apply). Response `queued=true` means the node is offline or in netboot recovery and the command waits for a managed-OS boot. 400 when the node's agent predates apply_access_config.

item.name: Apply access config to a netbooted node's disk

request.description:
Recovery-mode apply: while the node is netbooted into recovery, the agent mounts the target disk and writes the effective access configuration (users, keys, sudo, trusted CAs) into the installed OS; settings take effect on the next boot from that disk. Refused with 400 unless the node is currently in the recovery bootstrap. Omit target_device to auto-pick when the node reports exactly one disk (ambiguity is refused, never guessed); root_partition 0 lets the agent detect it. Requires agent >= 0.6.2 on the recovery image.

A node that is not netbooted into recovery answers 409 (code recovery_required).

Pushes the resolved access config to the agent. Requires agent >= 0.3.0; older agents are reported as skipped with reason agent_too_old rather than failed. An OFFLINE node does not fail — the command is queued and delivered on reconnect (success_count includes queued_count, which does NOT mean it has been applied). A newer config supersedes an older queued one for the same node.

Create an account-scoped secret or variable. kind is env|credential|opaque. sensitive defaults to true; only env entries may be non-sensitive (their value is returned by the API). tags categorize the entry and drive tag-based delivery. Name is unique per account.

The name is at most 255 characters, contains no "}" and does not start with "attr:"; a value is at most 64 KiB, and an env value has no line break (400, codes invalid_secret_name / invalid_secret_value).

query.description: delivered at this OU (incl. its nodes)

request.description: List secrets with server-side search, filters, sorting and pagination. Values are included only for non-sensitive entries. Response carries total/page/per_page.
The decrypted value is never returned; has_value reports whether one is set.

Update a secret. Omit value to keep it; empty string clears it. sensitive true->false is rejected (recreate instead); false->true is allowed. tags: omit = unchanged, [] = clear, list = replace.

A changed name and a new value follow the create rules (400); re-sending the stored name is always accepted.
Account tag vocabulary with usage counts (feeds the filter rail and tag suggestions).
Delivered-secret counts per OU (attachments to the OU itself or its nodes, tags expanded) + unattached + total.
Attach a secret to an organizational unit. Provide exactly one of ou_id or node_id.
Attach a secret directly to a node. Provide exactly one of ou_id or node_id.
List all attachments (OU or node targets) of a secret.
Detach a secret from a target by attachment ID.
List the secrets attached to an organizational unit. Values are never returned.
List the secrets attached directly to a node. Values are never returned.
Declarative replace of the node's DIRECT attachments: listed subjects are attached (idempotently), missing ones detached. OU-inherited secrets are untouched.

Replace a failed node with a spare one: clones the source's custom attributes onto the target, carries the hostname as an attribute, transfers OU membership, optionally starts a playbook on the target (template_id), then strips the source's attributes. The source node record is kept.
List a node's AD-style custom attributes (per-node key/value pairs backed by env-kind secrets attached to the node). Values are returned only for non-sensitive attributes.

Create or update one custom attribute of a node (unique per node+key). The value is delivered to the node's agent env keyed by the attribute key and resolves as {{node.attributes.<key>}} in playbooks. Turning a sensitive attribute non-sensitive is rejected; re-create instead.

The value is at most 64 KiB and has no line break (400, code invalid_attribute_value).
Remove one custom attribute of a node (the backing secret and its attachments).
Declarative replace of the OU's direct attachments.
Resolved effective set (direct + OU/root + tags expanded, node > OU > root; direct beats tag within a level) with source provenance. Values only for non-sensitive entries.
Effective set visible at an OU (own + root-inherited attachments, tags expanded) with provenance.

Create a tag with a name + palette color (or update the color of an existing tag). Membership stays on the secrets; this only sets presentation. Color must be a palette value (red|pink|purple|violet|blue|lightBlue|green|lime|yellow|orange); empty falls back to a deterministic default.
Rename a tag (cascades the string across every carrying secret and its attachments) and/or recolor it. Rename fails with 409 if the new name is already in use.
Remove a tag entirely: strip it from every secret, drop its attachments and delete the color row.
Attach a tag to an OU: every secret carrying it is delivered there (dynamic membership).
Attach a tag to a node.
Returns the catalog of block types available for workflow templates, including parameter schemas used to render editor forms and validate payloads
Create a workflow template; step slugs and payloads are validated against the block registry; optional ou_id scopes the template to an organizational unit (null = all nodes)
List workflow templates; optional filters: name, is_shortcut
Returns the built-in catalog of ready-made playbooks. Each entry carries the full portable document; instantiate one by posting its document to the import endpoint.

Creates a DRAFT playbook from a portable document (an exported playbook or a built-in starter). The graph is validated against the block registry; unresolvable account-scoped references (unknown image ids, missing secret names) are cleared/reported in the response's warnings array. Templates containing privileged blocks require playbook.author_privileged.

A body that does not decode answers 400 naming the JSON field and the kind it must be.
Get a workflow template by ID

Exports a playbook as a portable JSON document (kind orchestrator.playbook, schema_version 1: name, description, graph). Account-specific ids (OS images, SSH keys) are stripped. Served as a file download; the body round-trips through the import endpoint.
Update a workflow template; step slugs and payloads are validated against the block registry; optional ou_id scopes the template to an organizational unit (null = all nodes)
Delete a workflow template

Run a workflow template on a list of nodes

An empty node_ids answers 400 (code no_target_nodes).
List workflow executions; optional filter: template_id
Get a workflow execution with per-node progress

Settles a running or stuck execution so it stops counting against the account's active-execution cap (WORKFLOW_MAX_ACTIVE_EXECUTIONS_PER_ACCOUNT). Every unfinished node is failed and its in-flight device commands settled. Idempotent: cancelling a finished run changes nothing and reports settled=0. Requires playbook.run.
List per-node progress of a workflow execution
List the commands dispatched to one node during a workflow execution

item.name: Re-target a playbook to an organizational unit

request.description: Sets (or clears, with a null ou_id) the OU a playbook is scoped to, without rewriting the rest of the document
Retrieves a list of all master tokens for the authenticated account

Creates a new master token for agent authentication. Tokens expire 7 days after creation unless expires_at is set explicitly; the computed expiry is returned in the response.

A blank name or an expires_at that is not in the future answers 400 (codes invalid_name / invalid_expires_at).
Retrieves master token details by ID (without the actual token value)
Updates master token information (name, is_active, expires_at)
Deletes a master token by ID

item.name: Detach a secret or a tag

request.description: Removes one attachment by its id. The attachment's subject is a secret XOR a tag, which is why the same handler answers under both prefixes; the id in the path is the ATTACHMENT's, not the subject's.
Renames a tag (cascading the string across every carrying secret and its attachments) and/or updates its color. Rename fails if the new name is already in use.
Removes a tag entirely: strips it from every secret, drops its attachments, and deletes the color row.
List a tag's attachments

item.name: Attach a tag to a target

request.description: Attaches a tag to exactly one target (ou_id or node_id). Dynamic membership: every secret carrying the tag — now or later — is delivered there. Idempotent.
Retrieves a list of all SSH keys for the authenticated account

Creates a new SSH public key

Key content that is not an OpenSSH public key, or an unknown key_type, answers 400 (code invalid_ssh_key).

Generates a new ed25519 keypair server-side. The public part is stored (and deployed to nodes) like any SSH key; the private part is encrypted at rest and used by the platform for outbound SSH authentication (SSH-adopt). The private key is never returned — only the public part is downloadable.
Retrieves SSH key details by ID (without key content)

Updates SSH key information (alias, key content, or default status)

Replacement key content that is not an OpenSSH public key answers 400 (code invalid_ssh_key).
Deletes an SSH key by ID

Returns the public key text (authorized_keys line) so it can be placed into a device's authorized_keys — handy for pre-installing a connection key's public part on devices with password auth disabled.
Lists agent package versions available for install (local storage only).

Serves orchestrator agent packages (deb, rpm, tar.gz) by version, architecture, and package type. Files are stored in a flat structure with the pattern: orchestrator-agent_{version}_linux_{arch}.{ext}. The "latest" version is treated as a literal string, not resolved to the highest version.

Whether this instance can serve requests that touch its dependencies: a database ping plus free bytes AND free inodes on the storage path (replaced by a bucket reachability check when images live in object storage, because a statfs of a disk nothing writes to passes while every upload fails). Public and unauthenticated on purpose — an external uptime probe holds no token — and the body names which dependency is unhappy, never why. Cached for a few seconds.

Shell script that removes the orchestrator agent and everything it wrote from a device: `curl -fsSL https://<platform>/uninstall.sh | sudo sh`. It disarms the watchdog FIRST (an armed watchdog whose liveness file goes stale reboots the machine), then stops and purges the package and its state. SSH access artifacts are left alone unless `--purge-access` is given, and that is refused if it would remove the last way in.

item.name: Corresponding-source offer: list the published files

request.description: PUBLIC, tokenless. Plain-text listing of the corresponding-source bundle for the recovery image this install distributes (GPLv2 section 3, equivalent access): one line per file with name, size in bytes and the SHA-256 digest read from the `SHA256SUMS` placed beside the files (`-` when not listed). An install that publishes no offer (SOURCE_OFFER_DIR unset) answers 404 with a plain-text body saying so. Per-IP rate limited like the other public root routes.

PUBLIC, tokenless. Serves one file of the offer as an inert attachment (`application/octet-stream`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`) with Range requests supported, so a multi-hundred-megabyte archive can be resumed. The name is a bare file name as shown by the listing: a path separator or `..` is refused as 404, and only a regular file in the offer directory is served.

item.name: Utilities
item.description: OU-assignable software roles (docs/UTILITIES-PLAN.md): a static catalog, assignments (one utility x one target x one config), per-node effective view and explicit applies. Unassign is retain — deleting an assignment dispatches nothing.

request.description: Static utility registry: ids, consent class, dependencies, param schemas (workflow-block shape).
Every assignment of the account.
Per-OU assignment counts for the OU rail facet.

Assign a utility to an OU (ou_id), a node (node_id), the whole account (account_wide), or none of them (unassigned). 409 code utility_assignment_duplicate when the (utility, target) pair already exists. The OU target is a SET (ou_ids); legacy ou_id is still accepted and merged. 409 also answers an OU-overlap: no two assignments of one utility may share a unit.
One assignment row.
Edits config/enabled; the scope is replaced only when retarget=true (a config edit must not silently re-scope).
Dispatches the wholesale apply to every node the assignment reaches, bounded by the per-account concurrent-applies cap; nodes past the bound are reported deferred.
Removes the row. Unassign-is-retain: nothing is dispatched, software stays on devices unmanaged.
The node's resolved utility set with provenance (node/OU/account) and per-utility ladder status.

Per-utility rollup across the unit and its child units: applied / update_pending / failed / declared, out of the nodes the utility RESOLVES to. That count is not the unit's node count — a nearer assignment on a node overrides the unit's.
Resolves the node's set and dispatches ONE wholesale apply_utility_config command.
